summary.headline: Shilchar FY26 revenue INR652 crore (+5%) and EBITDA margin 29%, but Q4 EBITDA margin fell to 21% on deferred Middle East and US shipments and oil-led input inflation.
summary.overview: FY26 revenue from operations was INR652 crore (about 5% growth), EBITDA INR190 crore (29% margin) and PAT INR158 crore (+8%, EPS INR138). Q4 FY26 was weak: revenue INR152 crore, EBITDA margin 21%, PAT INR28 crore, as a large March export volume (INR35-40 crore) could not be shipped due to West Asia logistics disruption and US tariff uncertainty had slowed order intake earlier. Management says these were temporary, dispatches to the Middle East resumed in April, and it is seeking price revisions from customers for raw material inflation (oil roughly doubled since February, other commodities up 10-25%). FY27 guidance is INR800-850 crore revenue with margins targeted at 29-31%, and the Gavasad expansion (6,500 MVA, total 14,000 MVA) is due for commissioning in April 2027.

financial_highlights.change: down roughly 7-8 percentage points vs prior quarters per analyst; management said margin would have matched Q1-Q3 without March disruption

financial_highlights.value: Export about INR52 crore; domestic about INR100 crore

segments.name: Domestic transformers (incl. renewables/solar & wind)
segments.commentary: Q4 domestic revenue about INR100 crore; domestic renewable transformer order inflows described as strong, with India commissioning 55 GW renewables in FY26. Price revisions being secured from domestic customers, with at least a couple agreed.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Q4 export revenue about INR52 crore, with about INR35-40 crore of March shipments deferred. Middle East was about 30% of FY25-26 revenue; US was 18-19% of FY26 revenue. Export share of current INR452 crore order book is about 30-32%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target INR800-850 crore; management said it is conservative and could reach INR900 crore, with the INR800 crore figure described as the floor it is confident of.
FY27 volume target about 7,000 MVA vs about 6,000 MVA dispatched in FY26.
Q1 FY27 described as a normal quarter; no April actuals disclosed. Management expects growth to resume from the coming quarter.
EBITDA margin target for FY27 of 29-31%, with management saying it will try to maintain or increase margins.

Expansion (Gavasad expansion 3): 6,500 MVA, total 14,000 MVA, commissioning April 2027, capex about INR120 crore funded from internal accruals. Full benefit expected in FY29-FY30; power transformer approvals (up to 160 MVA, 220 kV class) need registration and customer audits.
capex_capacity: Current installed capacity 7,500 MVA; FY26 dispatches about 6,000 MVA (79% utilisation on a dispatch basis). Management said production utilisation is higher, with closing stock carried into FY27.

Gavasad expansion 3: adds 6,500 MVA, taking total to 14,000 MVA; commissioning targeted April 2027; civil foundation complete, PEB erection and utility work in progress, major production equipment ordered; capex about INR120 crore funded from internal accruals.
New facility can make transformers up to 160 MVA, 220 kV class; until power transformer approvals come through, it will produce solar and wind transformers.
Management said it would plan further expansion beyond 6,500 MVA and announce it later; once fully utilised, the company could reach about INR1,500 crore turnover.
Current power transformer lead time is 12-16 weeks. Bushings are sourced from Yash Highvoltage (Vadodara); China imports are also planned.
demand_pricing: FY27 order book about INR452 crore, about 30-32% export; management said FY27 order visibility is roughly INR800 crore, with robust domestic and export inquiries.

Price revisions sought from almost all customers for raw material inflation: oil up about 100% since February, other commodities up 10-25%. Some customers have agreed, others are in discussion; for fixed-price orders the company is invoking force majeure, while PV-clause orders pass through prices at dispatch.
Transformer oil is 8-12% of transformer cost. Company says it books copper or aluminium when orders are won, but this time suppliers also could not hold prices.
US tariffs were cut to about 10% from 50% (announced August 2025), and management says it is now winning US orders again. Management expects US export growth over the next 2-3 years.

Management says the competitive situation is good, with no overcapacity seen in distribution transformers. It also said new inquiries will be quoted at higher prices reflecting current raw material costs.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the gross margin compression, and are price hikes being accepted?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower export mix in March (deferred shipments) changed the raw material ratio, and oil prices spiked in March. Price increase discussions are active with almost all customers; some have agreed and supply has resumed for them.

qa_highlights.question: Can the INR80-90 crore lost Q4 sales be recovered in Q1, and what is the FY27 target?
qa_highlights.answer: Shipping has resumed and deferred transformers are going out. The FY27 target is INR800 crore, which management says it is confident of; Q1 will be a normal quarter, but no figure was given for the first half.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY27 guidance lowered from INR850-900 crore to INR800 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is taking a conservative stance; INR800-850 crore is the expected range and INR900 crore is possible given past beats.

qa_highlights.question: Why did utilisation rise only about 2 points (77% to 79%) if demand is strong, and can 100% be reached?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation is on a dispatch basis; the Middle East shipment delay cost roughly 2-3 points, so 82-83% was possible otherwise. Management aims for 90-95%, not 100%; the analyst's implied-realisation math (about INR11 lakh per MVA) pointed to near-100% utilisation, which management called a thumb-rule estimate.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the US and Middle East business is there, and what is the expected export outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: US was 18-19% of FY26 revenue. Middle East was about 30% of FY25-26 revenue. The current order book is about 30-32% export.

qa_highlights.question: Does the company have a hedging or price-escalation structure?
qa_highlights.answer: Orders are usually hedged by booking copper or aluminium on receipt. This time suppliers also demanded price increases, which management called force majeure. Some orders have PV escalation clauses; fixed-price orders are being renegotiated.

risks_watch: Customer price revisions: some fixed-price orders are unresolved, and margin recovery depends on how many customers accept.
Oil and commodity inflation (oil about +100%, other commodities +10-25%) could persist or reverse; management said it cannot predict this.
Middle East shipping normalisation and the ~INR35-40 crore of deferred March exports; April actuals were not disclosed.
Utilisation risk: FY26 dispatches were 79% of 7,500 MVA, and the FY27 volume target of 7,000 MVA needs strong execution.
Expansion execution (April 2027 commissioning) and 220 kV power transformer approvals, plus new capacity from peers.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and the order book, but guarded on near-term margins and figures: management declined to give April actuals, gave no first-half split, and kept guidance at the conservative INR800 crore end. Management blamed the Q4 miss on external factors it describes as temporary.

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided INR800-850 crore (floor INR800 crore, about 23-30% over FY26's INR652 crore, though guidance was cut from INR850-900 crore), volume ~7,000 MVA vs ~6,000 MVA, backed by INR452 crore order book and Gavasad-3 (6,500 MVA, April 2027, a 4-quarter lag), but the 8% figure in the call metadata is inconsistent with the 23-30% implied by the guidance range, so I used the stated FY26 grow
